Doherty made the allegation in a post on X on Sunday, after accusing Laoye of reproducing almost identical wording in his reaction to the incident, which occurred on Saturday, November 21. item.title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added. item.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
item.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians. item.title: Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation
item.description: The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State. The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit. The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria. She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation. She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek. According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts. “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. She described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive the encounter in her thoughts. The woman said the incident happened a week before she made the allegation public but explained that she waited until she had left Nigeria before speaking about it. She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the traditional ruler, although she did not provide evidence of such incidents. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added. Her allegation has generated reactions on X, with some users expressing concern and demanding accountability. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation. item.title: 70-year-old woman rescued after falling into 60ft well in Lagos
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni A 70-year-old woman has survived after accidentally falling into a 60-foot-deep well at Oworonshoki, Kosofe Local Government Area of Lagos State. The incident occurred in the early hours of Sunday at 37, Abiola Street, prompting a distress call to the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service. Firefighters from the Oworonshoki Fire Station promptly responded to the call and successfully rescued the septuagenarian alive. The rescue operation was concluded after the victim was stabilised and handed over to her family. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, who confirmed the incident, said the woman was responding to treatment as of press time. item.title: NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests
item.description: … 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight months By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enforcement against unsafe and substandard regulated products. The agency disclosed that it carried out 5,542 enforcement activities, including 213 raids, between January and August 2026, while 179 premises were shut and 221 sanctions imposed. The figures formed part of major regulatory milestones presented by NAFDAC at the International Pharmaceutical Regulators Programme (IPRP) Management Committee Meeting in Prague, Czech Republic, held from November 18 to 19, 2026. The agency also reported progress in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, disclosing that more than 70 per cent of finished pharmaceutical products covered by its 5+5 policy and Ceiling 36 are now being manufactured in Nigeria. The development is expected to reduce dependence on imported medicines and strengthen the country’s medicine security. In its regulatory update, NAFDAC said it had sustained its World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 3 status and was working towards attaining Maturity Level 4, the highest level of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool. It identified digital innovation as a critical component of the transition, citing the Integrated Regulatory Information Management System (IRIMS), Performance Management System (i-PMS), GMP Inspection (GMPi), Application and AI-assisted Technical Screening Tools (TST), and the revised Med Safety App. The revised application is designed to strengthen the reporting of adverse drug reactions and substandard and falsified medical products. NAFDAC also highlighted Nigeria’s growing influence in African pharmaceutical regulation, noting that it had emerged as a reference National Regulatory Authority, hosting regulatory authorities from Uganda, The Gambia, Mozambique and Côte d’Ivoire for technical capacity building and institutional benchmarking. Another milestone was Nigeria’s ratification of the African Medicines Agency (AMA) Treaty, with the instruments of ratification deposited on October 25, 2026. The agency said the achievements reflected the strategic leadership of its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, and ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity, promote science-based regulation and deepen international regulatory cooperation. NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health, strengthening Nigeria’s pharmaceutical industry and positioning the country as a leading regulatory authority in Africa. item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has called for an investigation into Friday’s fatal boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, urging the Federal and State Governments to strengthen safety measures on the nation’s waterways to prevent further loss of lives. Atiku said the tragedy, which claimed several lives, highlighted the risks faced by millions of Nigerians who rely on boats for daily transportation, particularly in riverine communities, and called for urgent government action to protect them. In a statement on Sunday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged the affected communities into mourning. He said the victims were travelling to honour a departed loved one when the accident occurred. “What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters,” Ologbondiyan said. “Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. No words can adequately capture the depth of grief now hanging over the affected communities.” Ologbondiyan commended local divers, the Marine Police, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other emergency responders for their efforts in the search and rescue operations. He, however, called for a thorough investigation into the cause of the mishap and stricter enforcement of regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices. He said preventing similar accidents would require sustained government investment in safer water transportation. “The Federal and State Governments must prioritise the provision of standard and well-maintained boats, adequate life jackets, functional jetties and properly trained boat operators across riverine communities,” he stressed. “For millions of Nigerians in the Niger Delta and other riverine areas, water transportation is not a luxury; it is a daily necessity. Their safety must never be treated as an afterthought.” He also urged the Federal Government, Bayelsa State Government and relevant humanitarian agencies to provide immediate assistance to survivors and bereaved families. Such assistance, he said, should include medical care, psychosocial support and financial help with the burial of victims. Atiku commiserated with the bereaved families, the people of Ayama and Ukubie communities and the Bayelsa State Government, while praying for the repose of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured. item.title: PSG confirm Desire Doue ruled out for months with torn ACL
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue has suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, the reigning French and European champions confirmed on Sunday. Doue, 21, went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half of Saturday’s 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice and was stretchered off in tears. The French international will undergo surgery before the end of the month, PSG added in a brief statement, without specifying the expected length of his absence, which is likely to be a matter of months. Doue looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow him to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG have also lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “It is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said on Saturday night. The French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. item.title: Church not a political party — Bishop Mike Okonkwo
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya. Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwavering love for the church. Members were said to have chanted “We love you” during the service. Bishop Mike Okonkwo of The Redeemed Evangelical Ministry, one of the spiritual fathers to the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, ministered on the theme “The Glory of The Church.” He charged members and ministers of the church to diligently keep the founder’s legacy and remain steadfast in Christ, reminding them of the advice he gave when the church founder died. “The responsibility fell on us to talk to… The only honour we can do for the sacrifice, the process, pains and everything that the man of God who is highly celebrated in this country is that his legacy must continue,” Bishop Okonkwo said. “And I told you that day that Fountain will never die. No matter the trial or temptation, this is a work that is solidly laid. The price has been paid; lives have been lost. There is no power of hell that would destroy this work. It will go from glory to glory.” Acknowledging recent online attacks, he said: “For the past one or two weeks, we have been literally battered on social media. There is nothing that has not been said, both what is true and what is not true. Phone calls from far and near: ‘Bishop Mike, where are you?’ You can’t separate me from Fountain; it’s not possible, because it’s a covenant established by God Himself. What affects Fountain affects me. Don’t think that I am just aloof. I said to myself, ‘God, you just have to give us wisdom.’” He added: “The day you fully understand the glory of God upon His church and what it takes to give birth to His church, then there is nothing from the gates of hell that will move you.” Bishop Okonkwo warned that the church is not a political party but God’s house. “The church is not a human institution; it’s God’s house; it belongs to Him. Think of the price that He paid for the church. We should all know that we are not for Tolu, Jimmy or the Board of Trustees; none of them died for you,” he said. “The church is not a political party because Jesus Christ’s life was involved. The church is not an ordinary thing. We must be careful that none of us is an instrument to destroy the church of Christ.” He declared that God is interested in the church and that its best days are ahead. “God is interested in this church, in case you don’t know. item.title: ABUAD warns students against cultism, cybercrime
item.description: Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future. The university also cautioned the students against examination malpractice, bullying and the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence, urging them to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, gave the warning at the institution’s 18th matriculation ceremony held over the weekend, where 2,442 students were formally admitted for the 2026/2027 academic session. The figure comprises 2,089 regular undergraduate students, 77 Open and Distance Learning students and 276 part-time students. Giving a breakdown of the undergraduate admissions, Olarinde said 306 students were admitted into the College of Social and Management Sciences, 307 into Sciences, 275 into Pharmacy, 684 into Medicine and Health Sciences, 171 into Law and 346 into Engineering. Addressing the students, the vice-chancellor described their admission as an opportunity that required discipline, responsibility and commitment to academic excellence. She urged them to be mindful of their associations, noting that their choice of friends could influence their habits, reputation, academic performance and future. According to her, university education goes beyond obtaining certificates to include character formation, emotional maturity, leadership development and the acquisition of values needed to contribute meaningfully to society. Olarinde urged the students to uphold the university’s philosophy of Labour, Service and Integrity, stressing that hard work, selfless service and honesty should guide their academic and professional pursuits. She also cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence and other emerging digital technologies, warning students not to present machine-generated materials or another person’s intellectual work as their original research. “The company you keep will influence your habits, attitude, reputation and ultimately your destiny. Surround yourselves with people who encourage learning, discipline, honesty and constructive ambition. “Stay away from cultism, substance abuse, bullying, examination malpractice, cybercrime and every other form of misconduct that can destroy your future and bring disrepute to your family and this university. “No momentary pleasure or misguided friendship is worth the sacrifice of your education, character or good name,” she said. On the use of artificial intelligence, the vice-chancellor said the technology could support research, improve productivity and create new opportunities for learning, but should not replace independent thinking, genuine scholarship or personal integrity. “Use digital tools responsibly. item.title: NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep
item.description: By Joseph Erunke Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs. The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. With food prices, transportation fares, accommodation costs and other essential expenses continuing to weigh heavily on households, the N20,000 monthly upkeep has increasingly come under scrutiny over its capacity to provide meaningful relief to beneficiaries. However, Sawyer said any decision to increase the allowance would have to be carefully weighed against the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme. He explained that while NELFUND was conscious of the need to improve students’ welfare, it could not make adjustments without considering the implications for the entire beneficiary population. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said. Beyond the proposed review by NELFUND, Sawyer disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was also considering an intervention aimed at providing students with more meaningful financial support to enable them to remain in school and successfully complete their academic programmes. Although he did not disclose the nature, scope or financial details of the proposed presidential intervention, the NELFUND chief suggested that the government was exploring ways to improve the level of assistance available to students. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said. item.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
item.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. item.title: Ogun PDP deputy guber candidate installed Akinkanju of Egbaland
item.description: By Jimoh Babatunde The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Deputy Governorship Candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has been installed as the first Akinkanju of Egbaland by the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, Okukenu IV. The installation took place at the Alake Palace on Saturday as part of activities marking the monarch’s 21st coronation anniversary. Sowunmi-Kolapo, who was previously honoured with the title of Iyalode of Ijemo, is also the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State. According to the palace, the new title, the first of its kind, was conferred on her in recognition of her contributions to the development of Egbaland and her commitment to the community. Oba Gbadebo urged her to remain committed to service, cultural preservation and the promotion of unity across Egbaland. The ceremony attracted prominent personalities, including government officials, business leaders, traditional rulers and politicians. The Ogun State PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other party leaders to celebrate with his running mate. Speaking at the reception held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo expressed gratitude for the honour, particularly acknowledging the Alake for the recognition. She also described the conferment as significant ahead of the 2027 governorship election, saying the people of Ogun State had spoken through the honour. The deputy governorship candidate maintained that the forthcoming election should transcend party affiliations, insisting that the people must resist any alleged attempt to undermine the state’s interests. “We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence. “I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty. “I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general. “Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said. Also honoured at the ceremony was Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, who was installed as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake. In his remarks, Adebutu congratulated his running mate and the other honourees, describing their recognition as well deserved. He said Sowunmi-Kolapo’s elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflected her years of service, loyalty, courage, motherly leadership and commitment to the unity and development of the Egba people. Adebutu also congratulated Obasanjo on her installation as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland, describing the honour as recognition of her distinguished public service and contributions to Egbaland and Nigeria. item.title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
item.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. item.title: ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos. Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church’s service, saying he had only heard about the injunction but had yet to receive the court order. “I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said. His remarks came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, made a surprise appearance at the service and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu. Thanking members for their continued support amid the controversy, Jimmy Odukoya said he appreciated their decision to attend the service despite the ongoing crisis. “In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation. He also reaffirmed his commitment to the church and its members, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.” Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that Okonkwo had already delivered the sermon, leaving him with little to add. “Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time. He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative. Earlier, Okonkwo told the congregation that he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit the church and bless its members amid the leadership crisis. “I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. item.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
item.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances. “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said. The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims. Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. item.title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
item.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners. Manchester City’s Italian manager Enzo Maresca gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on September 20, 2026. (Photo by PETER POWELL / AFP) The Fight Off the Pitch The bigger problem might be off the pitch entirely. Early in the 2026-27 season, an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. It ruled that the club used “sham” contracts with commercial partners to inflate revenues and cut costs by more than £900 million between 2009 and 2018. City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed.
